relevance_note: Case report of a GFAP R79H carrier with Alexander disease plus a literature table of R79H patients: 'In a six-yearold patient with a relatively mild form of Alexander disease, we detected a common R79H mutation in GFAP'.
method_note: Read the whole paper; a Python script built the JSON and transcribed Table 1 (columns: Patient number, present age(years)/sex, initial symptom /onset(months), onset of seizures(months), macrocephaly, ataxia, bulbar sign, spasticity, psychomotor deterioration, reference); output checked against the table by eye. Labels: Table 1 has a bare-number 'Patient number' column, so people are 'Table 1 #1'..'Table 1 #9'; #1 is 'our case', the first-hand patient of the narrative (text uses only role words). #2-#9 are literature patients from refs [4], [6], [7]; their GFAP variant (R79H) comes from the table title 'Clinical findengs in patients with an R79H mutation', a named group; missense from 'the GFAP R79H missense mutation'. Table symbols: the legend defines only 'NA=not apricable'; '-' is never defined as absent, so all '-' and NA cells are recorded as not reported; '+' cells are recorded as observed. The legend line is garbled/truncated ('...their length and weight were 2 SD below the mean. Thus they were classified in macrocephaly(+) group.'), so some macrocephaly(+) calls may be relative; patients not identifiable. 'bulbar sign' and 'psychomotor deterioration' were not mapped to dysphagia/dysarthria or cognitive decline checklist items (broader/different). Table 'delay' as initial symptom was taken as developmental delay. Patient #1: 'megalencephaly' is excluded in text but checklist 'macrocephaly or megalencephaly' left not reported (narrow vs broad); 'ataxic gait'/'intention tremor' absent but 'ataxia or cerebellar signs' left not reported; normal deep tendon reflexes and absent pathological reflexes do not settle 'spasticity or pyramidal signs', left not reported. 'Cranial nerve and deep tendon reflexes were normal' recorded as excluded abnormal cranial nerve findings / abnormal deep tendon reflexes as the paper words it; 'Metabolic screening did not reveal any abnormality' recorded as written (excludes nothing more specific). Ictal leftward eye deviation is recorded as seizure detail, not as an eye movement abnormality. Discrepancy: text calls patient #1 'a 6-year-old boy' (IQ at 5 years 11 months), while Table 1 gives present age 8.5 years; age at last evaluation recorded from the text (6 years). Onset recorded from text 'At five years of age' (table: seizure/61 months), although milestones were already slightly delayed. The Markdown renders the cDNA as '250G>A' (HTML entity); spans quote it verbatim, values give '250G>A'. Parents and the healthy elder brother were not tested or affected, so they get no rows. Ages for #2-#9 are in years (age) and months (onset), per the column headers quoted as second spans; '<18' and '12〜24' seizure onsets have no ISO value. n_patients_reported and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: no explicit count or statement about re-reporting the first-hand patient.
